2607.05217.title: Curated retrieval versus open web search in public AI information services: a coverage-trust trade-off
2607.05217.paper_summary: Public institutions increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to answer citizens' questions, often pairing a curated knowledge base with live web search, yet whether the sources behind these answers can be trusted has received little empirical scrutiny. We report a pre-launch expert evaluation of Evrópuvefur, an independent, government-funded service run by the University of Iceland that answers questions about the European Union, conducted as Iceland prepared for its referendum of 29 August 2026 on whether to resume EU accession talks. Five domain experts produced 551 evaluations of 449 AI-generated answers, scoring each against a seven-criterion quality rubric and, separately, flagging individual cited sources. We compared two retrieval paths: a curated local corpus (RAG) and open web search. In more than a third of the reviewed web-search answers (35%, 65 of 187), at least one cited source was flagged, almost always as untrustworthy or irrelevant; curated sources were flagged far less often and only for being out of date. Web search answered more questions, but at the cost of source quality; the curated corpus was trustworthy yet limited in coverage, and the model declined to respond when it fell short. The citation mix also passed over strong sources: across all 287 web-search answers, the system never cited RÚV, the public broadcaster and the country's most widely used news source. A companion prompt ablation shows how weak prompt-level steering is: a trusted-domain list in the system prompt raised the share of citations to listed domains only from 12% to 21%. Fluency and topical fit did not predict source trustworthiness. We argue that source trustworthiness is a measurable yet largely invisible dimension of information quality in public AI services, and we discuss transparency-oriented responses and their trade-offs.
2607.05217.paper_summary_zh: 公共機構越來越多地使用大型語言模型（LLMs）來回答公民的問題，通常將經過精選的知識庫與即時網路搜索相結合，但這些答案背後的來源是否可信卻鮮有實證檢驗。我們報告了一項針對Evrópuvefur的預發佈專家評估，這是一項由冰島大學運營的獨立政府資助服務，旨在回答有關歐盟的問題，該評估是在冰島為2026年8月29日是否恢復歐盟入會談判的公投做準備時進行的。五位領域專家對449個AI生成的答案進行了551次評估，根據七項標準質量評分，並單獨標記了個別引用的來源。我們比較了兩條檢索路徑：一個經過精選的本地語料庫（RAG）和開放的網路搜索。在被審查的網路搜索答案中，超過三分之一（35%，187個中的65個）至少有一個引用的來源被標記，幾乎總是被視為不可信或不相關；經過精選的來源則較少被標記，僅因為過時而被標記。網路搜索回答了更多問題，但以來源質量為代價；經過精選的語料庫是可信的，但在覆蓋範圍上有限，當模型無法滿足要求時會拒絕回答。引用的組合也忽略了強有力的來源：在所有287個網路搜索答案中，系統從未引用RÚV，這是公共廣播公司，也是該國使用最廣泛的新聞來源。伴隨的提示消融顯示提示級別的引導是多麼薄弱：系統提示中的受信領域列表僅將引用到列出領域的比例從12%提高到21%。流暢性和主題契合度並未預測來源的可信度。我們認為來源的可信度是一個可測量但在公共AI服務中大多隱形的信息質量維度，我們討論了以透明度為導向的應對措施及其權衡。
